name: JusPrin release build

# One platform of a JusPrin release, called by jusprin_release.yml.
#
# The build is OrcaSlicer's: its dependency workflow (build_deps.yml), cached
# under the key OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml uses, and its build
# scripts. Only the packaging is JusPrin's (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging).
# OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml can't be reused as it is: its Linux step looks
# for OrcaSlicer_Linux_V<version>.AppImage, which a JusPrin build never
# writes, and its packaging steps name everything OrcaSlicer.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      os:
        required: true
        type: string
      # x64 (Windows), arm64 or x86_64 (macOS); empty for Linux amd64, as in
      # OrcaSlicer's build_all.yml.
      arch:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      version:
        required: true
        type: string

jobs:
  cache:
    name: Find the deps cache
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.os }}
    outputs:
      key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
      path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
      hit: ${{ steps.lookup.outputs.cache-hit }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'
      - name: Compute the key
        id: key
        shell: bash
        env:
          # As in OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml. The macOS and Linux trees are
          # OrcaSlicer's and share its cache; OrcaSlicer builds Windows with clang-cl,
          # so JusPrin's cl tree is cached on its own.
          cache_os: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && format('{0}-{1}', inputs.os, inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && format('windows-{0}-msvc', inputs.arch) || format('linux-clang{0}', inputs.arch && format('-{0}', inputs.arch) || '')) }}
          dep_folder: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && format('/{0}', inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64') && '-arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep' || '/OrcaSlicer_dep' }}
        run: |
          echo "key=${cache_os}-cache-orcaslicer_deps-build-${{ hashFiles('deps/**') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Relative to the workspace, as build_deps.yml takes it.
          echo "path=deps/build${dep_folder}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Look the cache up
        id: lookup
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
          lookup-only: true

  deps:
    name: Build deps
    needs: cache
    if: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.hit != 'true' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_deps.yml
    with:
      cache-key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
      cache-path: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
      valid-cache: false
      os: ${{ inputs.os }}
      arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
      # cl under the Visual Studio generator, which JusPrin's Windows build uses.
      compiler: msvc
      # Stops build_deps.yml before it calls OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      build-deps-only: true
    secrets: inherit

  build:
    name: Build JusPrin
    needs: [cache, deps]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.cache.result == 'success' && (needs.deps.result == 'success' || needs.deps.result == 'skipped') }}
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.os }}
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - name: Load the deps
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
          fail-on-cache-miss: true

      # The same CMake as OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      # The Agent and Home pages are built with npm (JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt).
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # Windows
      - name: Set up MSVC
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        uses: microsoft/setup-msbuild@v3

      - name: Install NSIS
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: choco install nsis

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml calls build_win.bat, but with cl rather than
        # clang-cl. -i installs into build\OrcaSlicer, which the packaging reads.
        run: |
          $deps = (Split-Path "${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}").Replace('\', '/')
          .\build_win.bat -s -i --arch ${{ inputs.arch }} --build-dir build --deps-dir $deps --msvc --msbuild

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/windows_package.ps1 -BuildDir build -Version $env:VERSION `
            -Arch "${{ inputs.arch }}" -OutDir dist

      # macOS: each architecture is built here; jusprin_release.yml joins them
      # into the universal app and the disk image.
      - name: Prepare the Mac
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install libtool
          mkdir -p "${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/${{ inputs.arch }}"
          # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml does, for disk space: keep only the
          # selected Xcode.
          xcode=$(basename "$(cd "$(xcode-select -p)/../.." && pwd -P)")
          sudo find /Applications -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "Xcode_*.app" ! -name "$xcode" -exec rm -rf {} +
          sudo rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Caches/*

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: ./build_release_macos.sh -s -n -x -j 3 -a ${{ inputs.arch }} -t 10.15

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          tar -czf "dist/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_${{ inputs.arch }}.tar.gz" -C "build/${{ inputs.arch }}" OrcaSlicer

      # Linux
      - name: Install the build packages
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        uses: ./.github/actions/apt-install-deps

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          # -s builds the slicer and lays out build/package; JusPrin's AppImage
          # replaces OrcaSlicer's (-i).
          ./build_linux.sh -srlL
          ./scripts/check_appimage_libs.sh ./build/package ./build/package/bin/orca-slicer

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/appimage.sh build/package "$VERSION" \
            "dist/JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_V${VERSION}${{ inputs.arch && format('_{0}', inputs.arch) || '' }}.AppImage"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.arch || 'x64' }}
          path: dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          # The release keeps the files; these only carry them to it.
          retention-days: 7

From 2026-11-08, JusPrin app work lands on `jusprin-dev`. Kenneth: "branch out a jusprin-dev from the upstream merge commit, and use this branch as the dev branch". It starts at `975c703f08` (the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 into ui-walkthrough) and contains `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those. AGENTS.md's "Branches" section records this. `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1. Server code in tsd-enterprise goes straight to `master` (2026-11-06 rule, unchanged).

History: 2026-11-06 `jusprin-newui-integration`; 2026-11-07 `ui-walkthrough`; 2026-11-08 `jusprin-dev`.

`main`, Kenneth 2026-11-08: "main will be the stable branch that doesn't allow force push ( except in some extreme circumstances when no other options are feasible). This is so that the users who clone our repo won't have to force pull." and "for now, it also double a release branch. But this rule is more flexible than the first one." GitHub branch protection on `main` blocks force pushes and deletion, admins included (enforce_admins). `main` moves forward from `jusprin-dev` only when a version is released; ask before fast-forwarding it. On 2026-11-08 Kenneth chose to leave `main` at 4da9d7beb4 until 2.0.0 ships, although that means the scheduled nightly keeps running `main`'s older file and doesn't build `jusprin-dev` until then. Start the nightly by hand on `jusprin-dev` with only `-f sign_macos=true`. GitHub runs scheduled workflows from `main`'s copy of the file, and validates dispatch inputs against it.

**Why:** the dev branch is the build Kenneth reviews; work on a side branch never reaches what he tests.

**How to apply:** Kenneth, 2026-11-08: "I want the main checkout to be always on jusprin-dev". Since then /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin holds `jusprin-dev`; byoai-newui was moved to its own branch `byoai-newui`. Git allows one checkout per branch, so never check `jusprin-dev` out in a worktree. Commit from a worktree of your own on its own branch or detached at the tip. Then bring the main checkout along so its files match the branch; moving the ref from elsewhere (update-ref, or a push without a pull) leaves the main checkout's `git status` showing the new commits as reversed. When pushing is asked: push to origin jusprin-dev, then `git -C /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin pull --ff-only` (Kenneth: "you just need to bring the local main checkout by pulling from the remote"). On 2026-11-06 he asked where the rule said that, then asked to remove it. Removed in 96c7bda756 on claude/first-run-fixes; the removal reached jusprin-newui in the squash b0a2fe3b08. Kenneth confirmed on 2026-11-06 evening that dropping the rule was on purpose.

**Why:** the rule text was mine, not his; he had agreed to one recommendation, not to a standing rule. See [[trace-a-rule-to-kenneths-words]].

**How to apply:** don't cite --no-ff-only as a project rule. When landing a branch, ask Kenneth how he wants it landed (merge or squash) unless he has said so for that branch.

71:If you are an AI agent working for a contributor, please follow these steps:
72-
73-1. Show the contributor this guide before you open a PR or post a comment.
74-2. Search open PRs for the same change before you start.
75-3. If the contributor already has several open PRs, wait until some are merged before you open another.
76-4. Before you change code, check `.claude/skills/` for a skill that matches the change, and follow it.
77-5. If the code can be tested, add an automated test, and check that it fails without the change and passes with it.
78-6. Ask the contributor to test the change by hand. For a bug fix, they should build the code without the change and reproduce the bug. Then they should build the branch and check that the bug is gone.
79-7. Write the PR description in the [PR template](.github/pull_request_template.md). A body passed with `gh pr create --body` replaces the template, so start from the template's text.
80-8. If you couldn't build or run something, say so in the PR.
81-
82-## After you open the PR
83-
84-- **Add labels.** A bot will comment with instructions. Reply with the labels from the table above, for example `/bot add-label bug-fix, UI/UX`.
85-- **Leave "Allow edits by maintainers" turned on**, so a reviewer can push small fixes directly.
86-- **Mark the PR ready for review when it's finished.** Draft PRs are not merged.

-- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. +  - Home has no way back. Its header is the lockup alone.

+  - Leaving a screen (the project, Print history): a 32 DIP `button.icon` with a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke and the 16 DIP Lucide `arrow-left`, at the window's top left, then 12 DIP to the screen's own title in Body Bold. The tooltip names where it goes ("Back to Home").

+  - A chat that fills the window for one task closes with the same outlined button holding `x`, then the task as its title: "Add a printer", "Connect <printer>", "<printer> settings" for Ask AI about printer settings, "<filament> settings" for Ask AI about filament settings. The tooltip names where it returns to when the app knows it ("Back to Prepare").

name: JusPrin release

# Builds JusPrin from one commit and uploads the files to a DRAFT GitHub
# release. It never publishes anything.
#
# - The version is the one in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp, and
#   the draft is tagged jusprin/v<version>, as JusPrin 1.4.0 was (the repo
#   still holds OrcaSlicer's own v2.x tags). GitHub creates that tag only when
#   the draft is published, by hand, on the Releases page. JusPrin's update
#   check reads the public release list, which never includes drafts, so
#   users see nothing until then.
# - It stops if that version is already released, is not above every
#   released JusPrin version, or its tag already exists
#   (Packaging/release.mjs), and if
#   Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md, the notes the draft starts with and
#   that the app shows under "What's new", is missing.
# - Running it again for the same version replaces the draft's files.
# - Files: Windows x64 installer and portable zip, macOS universal disk image,
#   Linux x64 AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - Only the release publisher can run it: the repo variable
#   JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER, or kennethjiang when it is unset.
# - Signing: macOS when "sign_macos" is ticked, with the Apple secrets JusPrin
#   1.x used. Windows builds are unsigned. An unsigned draft says so in its
#   title.
#
# Start it from Actions > JusPrin release > Run workflow (the file must also
# be on the default branch for that button), or by pushing a branch named
# jusprin-release/<anything>.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign_macos:
        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
        type: boolean
        default: false
  push:
    branches:
      - 'jusprin-release/**'

permissions:
  contents: write   # create the draft and upload its files
  actions: read

concurrency:
  group: jusprin-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: Check the version
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.check.outputs.tag }}
      prerelease: ${{ steps.check.outputs.prerelease }}
      draft_id: ${{ steps.check.outputs.draft_id }}
    steps:
      - name: Only the release publisher
        env:

input.content:
# Why the jusprin-dev nightly fails on macOS (2026-11-11)

Cause: GitHub-side. Every cancelled macOS job carries the annotation
"The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts"
plus "Due to capacity constraints, jobs targeting macOS arm64 runners may experience
longer queue times". GitHub cancels a job that gets no hosted runner within 15 minutes
(created 15:31:57, cancelled 15:46:58; same 15 min on 11-09 and 11-10). The "95 minutes"
was the whole run waiting for the Windows build; the macOS jobs died at 15 minutes.

Not the cause:
- main's scheduled run: it only runs one 8-second Linux job; it shares the concurrency
  group "jusprin-nightly" but finishes before the jusprin-dev run starts.
- Billing: org is on the free plan, repo public, all macOS minutes free (usage API, net $0).
- Our concurrency limit: free plan allows 5 macOS jobs; the run asks for 2 at a time.

Time of day: 7 runs started 22:00-08:30 UTC (11-08/11-09) got macOS runners in seconds;
3 runs started 15:30-17:45 UTC got none. Community threads report the same since
~2026-11-02 (github.com/orgs/community/discussions/211885, /212069), no GitHub answer.
This repo's cron schedules fire 7-10 h late (nightly cron 07:35 UTC fires 15:31-17:44),
landing the nightly in the worst window. Upstream OrcaSlicer's crons fire within minutes.

Change (branch claude/nightly-macos-runners, commit 05c9e48de1, not pushed):
jusprin_release_build.yml runs the macOS deps-cache lookup on ubuntu-24.04, as upstream's
build_check_cache.yml does. Five macOS runner acquisitions per nightly become three.
Verified the cache version hash matches the saved macOS entries.
